memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, "Get up early in the morning and confront Pharaoh as he goes to the river and say to him, 'This is what the Lord says: Let my people go, so that they may worship me. If you do not let my people go, I will send swarms of flies on you and your officials, on your people and into your houses. The houses of the Egyptians will be full of flies; even the ground will be covered with them.'"" - Exodus 8:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Again God sends Moses early in the morning, to the river, to confront Pharaoh at the place of his false worship. And again the same request: let my people go, so that they may worship me.

God is remarkably persistent. He has been refused repeatedly, insulted, and dismissed, and He still sends the message again.

That persistence is His mercy. Every fresh warning is another opportunity. Peter explains that the Lord's apparent slowness is patience, because He does not want anyone to perish (2 Pet 3:9).

There is a lesson for us in this too. If you have been praying for someone for years with no visible change, you are following God's own pattern. He does not give up quickly on hard hearts, and neither should we.

Notice also how ordinary the threat is. Not fire from heaven — flies. God does not need spectacular weapons. He can humble an empire with insects.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Whom have I given up on that God has not given up on?
2. Am I grateful for the times God gave me another warning instead of judgement?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for Your patience with me. Give me that same patience with the people I have stopped praying for. Amen.
